title: MATH 06-03 Mastery Challenge: Euler's Polyhedral Formula, Platonic Solids & Dual Polyhedra

questions.promptText: What does Euler's Polyhedral Formula state for any convex polyhedron with $V$ vertices, $E$ edges, and $F$ faces?
questions.explanation: Leonhard Euler proved in 1758 that for any simply connected convex polyhedron, $V - E + F = 2$.

questions.promptText: How many equilateral triangular faces does a regular Icosahedron possess?
questions.explanation: A regular icosahedron has 20 triangular faces, 30 edges, and 12 vertices.

questions.promptText: Find the exact volume of a regular tetrahedron with edge length $e = 6\text{ cm}$.
questions.explanation:
$V = \frac{e^3\sqrt{2}}{12} = \frac{6^3\sqrt{2}}{12} = \frac{216\sqrt{2}}{12} = 18\sqrt{2} \approx 25.4558\text{ cm}^3$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $\frac{216}{12}\sqrt{2} = 18\sqrt{2}$.

questions.promptText: Which Platonic solid is the dual polyhedron of the regular Hexahedron (Cube)?
questions.explanation: The Cube ($6F, 8V, 12E$) and Octahedron ($8F, 6V, 12E$) are duals of each other.

questions.promptText: A convex polyhedron has $30$ edges and $12$ vertices. How many faces does it have?
What is the total surface area of a regular tetrahedron with edge length $e = 4\text{ cm}$?
questions.explanation:
$A_s = e^2 \sqrt{3} = 4^2 \sqrt{3} = 16\sqrt{3} \approx 27.7128\text{ cm}^2$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $4^2 \sqrt{3} = 16\sqrt{3}$.

questions.promptText: What regular polygon forms each of the $12$ faces of a regular Dodecahedron?
questions.explanation: A regular dodecahedron has 12 identical regular pentagonal faces.

questions.promptText: Find the volume of a regular octahedron with edge length $e = 3\text{ cm}$.
questions.explanation:
$V = \frac{e^3\sqrt{2}}{3} = \frac{27\sqrt{2}}{3} = 9\sqrt{2} \approx 12.7279\text{ cm}^3$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $\frac{27}{3}\sqrt{2} = 9\sqrt{2}$.

questions.promptText: How many total edges $E$ does a regular Dodecahedron have?
questions.explanation: A dodecahedron has 12 pentagons with 5 edges each: $E = \frac{12 \times 5}{2} = 30$.

questions.promptText: Which of the Platonic solids is self-dual (meaning connecting its face centers produces the same geometric solid)?
questions.explanation: A tetrahedron has 4 vertices and 4 faces, making it self-dual.

questions.promptText: What is the sum of the plane face angles meeting at each vertex of a regular Octahedron?
questions.explanation: At each vertex of an octahedron, 4 equilateral triangles meet: $4 \times 60^\circ = 240^\circ$.

questions.promptText: A soccer ball (truncated icosahedron) has 12 regular pentagons and 20 regular hexagons. How many vertices $V$ and edges $E$ does it have?
questions.explanation:
$F = 12 + 20 = 32$. Edges $E = \frac{12(5) + 20(6)}{2} = \frac{60 + 120}{2} = 90$. Vertices $V = 2 + E - F = 2 + 90 - 32 = 60$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $V = 60, E = 90$ (standard C60 fullerene / soccer ball).

questions.promptText: What is the ratio of the volume of a regular octahedron to the volume of a regular tetrahedron of the same edge length $e$?
questions.explanation: $V_{\text{octa}} = \frac{e^3\sqrt{2}}{3}$ and $V_{\text{tetra}} = \frac{e^3\sqrt{2}}{12}$, so $\frac{V_{\text{octa}}}{V_{\text{tetra}}} = \frac{1/3}{1/12} = 4$.

questions.promptText: What is the inradius $r$ of a regular octahedron with edge length $e = 6\text{ cm}$?
questions.explanation:
$r = \frac{e\sqrt{6}}{6} = \frac{6\sqrt{6}}{6} = \sqrt{6} \approx 2.4495\text{ cm}$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $\frac{6\sqrt{6}}{6} = \sqrt{6}$.

questions.promptText: Who was the ancient Greek philosopher in whose dialog Timaeus the five regular solids were associated with the classical elements (fire, earth, air, water, cosmos)?
questions.explanation: Plato (427–348 B.C.) described the five regular polyhedra in Timaeus, hence the name Platonic solids.

questions.promptText: Find the total surface area of a regular Icosahedron with edge length $e = 2\text{ cm}$.
questions.explanation:
$A_s = 5 e^2 \sqrt{3} = 5(2^2)\sqrt{3} = 20\sqrt{3} \approx 34.641\text{ cm}^2$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $5 \times 4 \times \sqrt{3} = 20\sqrt{3}$.

questions.promptText: Why are there EXACTLY FIVE regular convex polyhedra in 3-dimensional Euclidean space?
questions.choiceB: Because the sum of face angles meeting at a vertex must be strictly less than $360^\circ$, and at least 3 faces must meet at each vertex
questions.choiceC: Because only triangles and squares can form solids
questions.choiceD: Because higher polyhedra have curved surfaces
questions.explanation: Euclid proved in Elements Book XIII that only 5 combinations of regular polygons have vertex angle sums $< 360^\circ$ with $\ge 3$ faces per vertex.

questions.promptText: What is the circumradius $R$ of a regular Octahedron with edge length $e = 4\text{ cm}$?
questions.explanation: $R = \frac{e\sqrt{2}}{2} = \frac{4\sqrt{2}}{2} = 2\sqrt{2} \approx 2.8284\text{ cm}$.

questions.promptText: If the volume of a regular octahedron is $72\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}^3$, what is its edge length $e$?
questions.explanation:
$\frac{e^3\sqrt{2}}{3} = 72\sqrt{2} \implies e^3 = 216 \implies e = 6\text{ cm}$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $\sqrt[3]{216} = 6\text{ cm}$.

questions.promptText: How many vertices $V$ does a regular Dodecahedron have?
questions.explanation: A regular dodecahedron has 20 vertices, 30 edges, and 12 pentagonal faces.

questions.promptText: What is the dual polyhedron of the regular Dodecahedron?
questions.explanation: The Dodecahedron ($12F, 20V$) and Icosahedron ($20F, 12V$) are dual polyhedra.

questions.promptText: A geodesic dome is built by subdividing the faces of an Icosahedron into a grid of triangles. If each of the 20 faces is divided into 4 smaller triangles, how many triangular faces $F$ does the dome base structure have?
questions.explanation: $20 \times 4 = 80$ triangular faces (a 2-frequency geodesic sphere).
